question: Which tissue breaks down over time in a joint affected by osteoarthritis?
explanation: Osteoarthritis happens when the smooth articular cartilage protecting the ends of bones wears down over time. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why do bony growths called osteophytes form around joints in late-stage osteoarthritis?

options.A: Muscles around the joint contract tightly and pull the bone outward.
options.B: Chronic bacterial infection triggers excessive calcium deposits.
options.C: Synovial membranes overproduce thick fluid to lubricate bones.
options.D: The body attempts to repair joint damage caused by cartilage loss.

explanation: Bone spurs form because the body tries to stabilize a joint after it loses its protective cartilage cushioning. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h1)

question: Which group experiences a higher rate of osteoarthritis after middle age?
explanation: Hormonal shifts and ongoing joint stress mean women past menopause experience osteoarthritis more often than men of the same age. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h2)

question: How does extra body weight contribute to knee osteoarthritis?

options.A: By weakening the quadriceps muscles so they can no longer hold the kneecap
options.B: By circulating inflammatory antibodies that attack synovial lining cells directly
options.C: By placing continuous excessive mechanical load on weight-bearing joint surfaces
options.D: By blocking calcium absorption in the gastrointestinal tract and bones

explanation: Extra weight creates constant physical pressure that wears down the protective cartilage in weight-bearing joints much faster. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h2)

question: How long does morning joint stiffness typically last in osteoarthritis?
explanation: Osteoarthritis stiffness is brief upon waking and improves quickly with gentle movement, unlike inflammatory arthritis which lasts longer. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is crepitus when assessing a patient's knee joint?

options.A: A grating or cracking sound and feeling during joint movement
options.B: Sudden locking of the joint in a fully bent position
options.C: Severe fluid accumulation causing a soft, spongy swelling
options.D: Complete numbness of the skin overlying the kneecap

explanation: Crepitus occurs when rough, unprotected bone ends rub against each other inside a worn joint during movement. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h3)

question: Which imaging test is most commonly used to confirm osteoarthritis?
explanation: Standard X-rays clearly show common signs of osteoarthritis like joint space narrowing and bone spurs at a low cost. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why are routine blood tests ordered when evaluating suspected osteoarthritis?

options.A: To check if the patient has a bacterial bone marrow infection
options.B: To rule out systemic inflammatory or autoimmune joint disorders
options.C: To calculate the precise calcium content inside the synovial fluid
options.D: To measure the exact amount of remaining joint cartilage

explanation: Blood tests for primary osteoarthritis are usually normal, but they are necessary to rule out conditions like rheumatoid arthritis that need different care. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of early conservative management for osteoarthritis?

options.A: To completely regrow worn-out articular cartilage
options.B: To relieve pain and maintain functional joint mobility
options.C: To dissolve abnormal calcium deposits inside the bone marrow
options.D: To permanently cure the underlying degenerative process

explanation: Since damaged cartilage does not grow back, early treatment focuses on controlling symptoms and keeping the patient mobile. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h5)

question: Which intervention should a midwife prioritize first for an overweight patient with early knee osteoarthritis?

options.A: Strict bed rest to prevent any further friction on the bones
options.B: Immediate scheduling for total knee replacement surgery
options.C: Guided weight reduction and low-impact exercise education
options.D: Intravenous administration of high-dose systemic steroids

explanation: Lifestyle changes like weight loss and strengthening exercises reduce joint stress and form the foundation of osteoarthritis management. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h5)

question: How does using larger joints for daily tasks help manage osteoarthritis?

options.A: It distributes physical stress away from smaller, vulnerable joints.
options.B: It stimulates rapid repair of damaged cartilage surfaces.
options.C: It completely stops the formation of bony osteophytes.
options.D: It increases the volume of synovial fluid inside the knee.

explanation: Using larger joints and muscle groups reduces wear and tear on fragile or already damaged joints during daily activities. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful daily strategy for joint protection?

options.A: Using walking aids like a cane on the unaffected side
options.B: Maintaining a healthy body weight through balanced diet
options.C: Alternating periods of light activity with scheduled rest
options.D: Lifting heavy items entirely with delicate finger joints

explanation: Patients are advised to avoid straining small finger joints and instead use larger, stronger body structures to carry loads. [learn more](BMP216_U3_T7#BMP216_U3_T7_h6)
